releases.headline: The licence locks at the expiry minute, locks to one phone, and an expired customer can finally renew from inside the app
fixed: THE LICENCE NOW LOCKS HARD AT THE EXPIRY MINUTE. The app used to keep working for three more days, and an app left open past midnight carried on working on a licence that had already run out. There is no grace now: the expiry minute IS the lock minute.
THE APP CHECKS THE LICENCE AGAIN EVERY TIME IT COMES BACK TO THE FRONT and arms a watch for the exact expiry minute, so an app that is never backgrounded still locks itself on time.

AN EXPIRED LICENCE COULD NOT BE RENEWED FROM THE APP. The expired verdict threw the licence away with it, so the renewal button was never even drawn. The licence id is now carried on the expired verdict, the renewal is offered, and new time is added to the licence the customer already holds - no paid day lost.

A LICENCE KEY CAN NOW BE LOCKED TO ONE PHONE. A key is a string, so an unbound tester licence could be handed to a dozen people. The issuer can bind a licence to a device code (same id, same payment, same expiry - only the phone changes) and the app binds itself the first time it reaches the licence service.
A LICENCE LOCKED TO ONE PHONE CANNOT BE RE-POINTED: a second bind to a different phone is refused, so the lock cannot be walked around one phone at a time.
THE CLIENT NO LONGER SHOWS A STALE VERSION NUMBER - it read a hardcoded 1.5.0 while the APK was 1.7.x; it now reads the version compiled into the build.
THE ISSUER READS THE NEWEST ROW OF THE LEDGER for a licence rather than the oldest, so a renewal is measured from the expiry the customer actually holds.
EVERY BUILD NOW SAYS WHAT IT FIXED: the fix index ships inside the APK and the build refuses to ship unless its newest entry is this version and lists its fixes.

releases.name: GHVST (Android)
releases.headline: Six real defects found by reading the phone's own 277-turn chat log - and all six closed
fixed: THE DESKTOP-CLI LIE IS GONE. The tool schema advertised cli_install for opencode / codex / claude-code, which are desktop binaries: npm rejects them on Android with EBADPLATFORM. The tool now refuses them BEFORE any network work and names the Android-native route instead.

THE run_steps SEPARATOR. The model sent 'tool|;tool2|;tool3' while the parser only accepted ' ;; ', so the same broken batch was re-sent for six turns. ' |;' now normalises to ' ;; ' - and a bare ';' still does not split, because a real shell command contains one.

THE SANDBOX NO LONGER REFUSES THE APP'S OWN WORKSPACE. Measured on the device: the real workspace is the app's own external files dir, yet every read from it came back 'path escapes sandbox'. The allowed roots now include the external files dir and the private files dir, and the boundary is a path separator rather than a text prefix.

THE download_file SCHEMA NO LONGER LIES. It advertised a folder that cannot exist on the phone; it now says use the path the tool RETURNS, with the critical rule kept inside the 160-character on-wire cap.

THE CROSS-TURN LOOP IS KILLED. toolchain_audit x4, runtime_install x3 and run_steps x3 were repeating ACROSS turns where the in-turn breaker could not see them. Every failed call is now fingerprinted for the whole session and handed back with its real error text.

THE PHONE CAN BUILD A WEBSITE. web_scaffold writes a real project, web_serve runs it on the phone's own node (no npm package, so no EBADPLATFORM risk) and PROVES it with a real HTTP request to the running server, and web_stop kills it by its recorded PID.

releases.name: GHVST DevKit
releases.headline: The sovereign agent: an AI on the phone that actually does things, with a permission model that refuses the catastrophic instead of asking
fixed: CATASTROPHIC COMMANDS ARE REFUSED, NOT ASKED. Wiping a filesystem, formatting a disk, writing to a block device, a fork bomb, fastboot -w, flash all, a factory reset: DevKit will not run them and will not offer to, so there is no approval that could enable them.

DESTRUCTIVE COMMANDS ALWAYS ASK, EVEN WITH ALL ACCESS ON. Delete, uninstall, clear an app, change a system setting, pipe a download into a shell, force-stop, a destructive git command. 'ALWAYS' on the approval card trusts THAT rule, not the whole tool - trusting rm still cannot run rm -rf /.
APPROVALS ARE INLINE CARDS in the conversation - ALLOW ONCE / ALWAYS / DENY - showing the exact command, its arguments and the reason. Nothing hidden behind a dialog, nothing hidden by omission.

THE SHARED TERMINAL: the owner and the agent drive ONE shell - same directory, same exported variables, the real device shell (uid 2000) through Shizuku - with cwd, env and history persisting across sessions.

THE PIPELINE: fetch_binary pulls a file onto the phone, install_from_url pulls an APK and installs it with pm install -r, analyze_image reads a picture with the current vision model, send_file puts a file in Downloads and opens the share sheet. The agent never sends anything on its own.
THE VOICE ASSISTANT runs hands free - microphone, model, spoken answer, microphone again - and switches itself off after three failed recognitions so a broken recogniser can never loop forever.
NO ACCOUNT, NO SERVER, NO TELEMETRY: the licence is verified OFFLINE against a compiled public key and the owner's own NVIDIA NIM key is stored encrypted in the phone's Android Keystore.
